trigger: an unresponsive offline-hive mount (e.g. a dead network share) during the retry's Phase B

adjudication_rationale: put to the user as a three-way choice (disclose+defer / build the real fix now / narrow the retry's reach); directed to build the real fix rather than defer

policy_floor: ownership/lifetime defect: an unjoined, ambiguously-owned thread running plugin code that the agent can unmap (cpp-safety blocking contract)
trigger: a hive mount that outlives its 30 s bound while the agent stops and unloads the TAR module
classification_rationale: the unjoined thread runs plugin code after the owner's bounded wait; derived MEDIUM (I5, E5: a >30 s hang plus a stop in the window, impact a crash at shutdown), gated by the lifetime policy floor; nobody forced the scenario
summary: enum_registry_outbound_history abandons the bounded mount thread on TimedOut; the thread keeps running TAR code, TarPlugin::shutdown neither tracks nor waits for it, and the agent teardown dlcloses/FreeLibraries the plugin. Fixed in 84e409f4b and refined in 294f472ba after the adversarial review (which showed that a mount that COMPLETES leaves a detached worker destroying a plugin-resident closure after publishing its result): the plugin module is pinned (GetModuleHandleExW with PIN, once, checked) before the FIRST bounded mount, no mount is tried if the pin fails, and a timeout stops the walk. Accepted residuals, recorded here: the DLL stays loaded until process exit; the stuck thread holds the process-wide offline-hive mutex and leaves SeBackup/SeRestore enabled until the mount returns; it occupies one of the primitive's 64 slots. The banner no longer cites dism_bounded_call.hpp as its pattern (that header keeps its work in agent-core). Chosen with Alex over moving the mount into agent-core (a redesign) and over a recorded acceptance.

trigger: one hung offline profile in the walk
classification_rationale: correctness of the retry accounting; the walk's wait is no longer 30 s per profile
summary: After one timeout every later offline profile queued behind the stuck mount (it holds the offline-hive mutex), timed out in turn and was charged an attempt it never made; a Rejected call (fn never ran) was charged too. Fixed in 84e409f4b (refined in 232d2a765, 294f472ba and 435cef84a after later gates): decide_mount_call stops the walk after the first TimedOut or Rejected, the remaining profiles carry attempted=false, which apply_outcomes retains without a bump, and the first pass still seeds them so they are retried, not lost.

summary: apply_outcomes retained a cap-cut read unchanged, so the profile retried forever against the 'total number of acquisitions' contract in the README and banner. Codex graded this HIGH (I5(b)); the reviewer MEDIUM, since the rule needs persistent work on a path shared with revocation, enforcement, audit or retention and this is one short daily read. Fixed in 84e409f4b (refined in 232d2a765, 294f472ba and 435cef84a after later gates): a cap-cut read is an attempt like any other and is abandoned at the maximum (token row_cap).
